releasePlan.notes: Roles: enable-backend-status-error-rate = killswitch; enable-backend-status-latency = pause; enable-backend-status-success-rate = monitoring. The feature is net_new (control renders no backend-status element), so the error and success metrics are ONE-ARMED: only v1 traffic can emit them. The project has no otel* or $ld:telemetry autogenerated global metrics to guard with instead, so feature-scoped metrics are the documented fallback. sentry-errors-binary / sentry-errors-count were considered and rejected: only the Flask backend initializes Sentry, so this Node frontend can never emit sentry-errors. The latency metric is deliberately TWO-ARMED (server-side page render duration, emitted on control and v1 alike) and therefore a valid comparison; browser-side status-fetch duration is intentionally NOT folded into it, because mixing a treatment-only distribution into the same metric would poison the comparison. Residual gap: no guardrail covers client-perceived latency of the new fetch.
